scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Umxhentso originates from the Xhosa people of South Africa, with its roots deeply tied to the Transkei homeland in the Eastern Cape.
It has historically served as a central component of Xhosa ceremonies and the work of traditional healers.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Umxhentso is performed at weddings (Umdudo), initiation ceremonies for healers (Intlombe), rites of passage for boys (Umguyo), and ritual ceremonies for women (Umngqungqo).
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves barefoot stomping and vigorous upper-body movement.
A key technique is ukutyityimba, which involves shaking the thoracic region and the upper body.
It is often accompanied by rhythmic clapping.
Watch for Ukutyityimba.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music includes the Uhadi musical bow, drum beats, and the use of a whistle called an Impempe, made from Ingcongolo reed.
Vocal accompaniment is provided through the composition and singing of theme songs called ukombela.
Listen for the Uhadi musical bow, Drum, Impempe (reed whistle).

The music is characterized by the resonant twang of the Uhadi bow, the steady beat of drums, and the piercing, high-pitched sound of the Ingcongolo reed whistle, all layered under rhythmic clapping and vocal chanting.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Umxhentso is used in initiation ceremonies and by traditional healers (Amagqirha) for spiritual work; outsiders should respect the ritual nature of these performances.
